title: Recent advances in luminescent lanthanide based Single-Molecule Magnets
claim: Across the compiled Dy3+ examples the magnetic effective barrier is usually lower than the first-excited-state gap measured by luminescence, showing that dynamic magnetometry underestimates the crystal-field gap when extra relaxation channels operate.
explanation: The authors state this as a pattern from Table 1. Exceptions where the magnetic barrier is much larger than the first gap are interpreted as TA-QTM through higher states (for example the bis(methanediide) Dy complex). A few cases are close or inverted, so the trend is usual rather than absolute.
scope: Dy3+ luminescent SMMs for which both magnetic Δ and spectroscopic Δ_Orbach are reported.
conditions: Comparison of ac magnetometry with emission-derived crystal-field gaps.
caveats: Not every entry follows the inequality; inequivalent sites can also occur in mononuclear complexes and undermine a single-gap comparison.
